VirtueVigil has now reviewed over 650 films using our dual-scoring methodology, which measures the density and intensity of both woke content and traditional values content independently. Most of our listicles rank films from most woke to least. This one runs the other direction. These are the 25 films in our database with the widest traditional margins: the films where courage, sacrifice, faith, family, duty, and earned redemption are not window dressing but the entire architecture of the story.

The scoring is not a quality rating. Some of these films are masterpieces. Some are flawed. The score reflects ideology, not craft. A +45 traditional margin means the film's traditional values content outweighs its woke content by 45 points on our 100-point dual scale. That is not a close call. That is a film built on traditional moral foundations from the ground up.

What stands out in the data: faith-based films and war films dominate the top tier. The Passion of the Christ, Reagan, and Sound of Hope all crack the top 25, as do American Sniper, 13 Hours, and Saving Private Ryan. Sports films produce three entries (Miracle, Hoosiers, Rocky). Animation shows up five times (SpongeBob, Ne Zha 2, Paddington 2, Toy Story, Solo Leveling). The most recent film on the list is Exit 8, a 2026 Japanese psychological horror film that is both one of the best-reviewed horror films of the year and one of the most traditional films we have ever scored. Not a single film on this list was made by a studio trying to check progressive boxes. Some were made by studios actively trying not to. The list runs from #1 (widest traditional margin) to #25 (strongest traditional margin in the fourth quartile). Every entry links to its full VirtueVigil review with complete category breakdowns.

#1: The Passion of the Christ (2004)

STRONGLY TRADITIONAL TRAD: 45.3 WOKE: 0.0 MARGIN: +45.29 TRADITIONAL

Genre: Biblical Drama • Platform: Theatrical (Newmarket Films / Icon Productions)

Mel Gibson did not make a movie. He made an act of witness. Shot in Aramaic, Latin, and Hebrew with no hand-holding for the uninitiated, The Passion of the Christ is a devotional work aimed at believers who want to feel what the Passion actually cost. Jim Caviezel endures real physical suffering on screen in one of the most committed performances in cinema history. The film grossed $612 million on a $30 million budget, becoming the highest-grossing R-rated film in American history. The audience that found this film was the audience Hollywood had been ignoring: practicing Christians who wanted their faith taken seriously on screen, not sanitized or updated for modern sensibilities, but rendered with theological seriousness and real filmmaking craft.

#2: The Shawshank Redemption (1994)

STRONGLY TRADITIONAL TRAD: 47.3 WOKE: 5.2 MARGIN: +42.14 TRADITIONAL

Genre: Drama / Prison • Platform: Theaters (1994) / Home Video / Streaming

The most conservative film ever voted the greatest movie of all time. Frank Darabont's adaptation of Stephen King's novella follows Andy Dufresne through two decades of wrongful imprisonment, sustained by patience, intelligence, and an almost supernatural commitment to hope. Red's arc is the Redemptive Arc in its purest form: a man who has done terrible things finds salvation through honest self-confrontation. The prison is a moral universe governed by objective good and evil, and the ending on the Zihuatanejo beach is the Forgiving Heart finding its reward. The film holds the #1 position on IMDb and has done so for over two decades.

#3: Reagan (2024)

STRONGLY TRADITIONAL TRAD: 44.3 WOKE: 2.4 MARGIN: +41.88 TRADITIONAL

Genre: Biography/Drama/History • Platform: Theatrical

Sean McNamara's Reagan is not a biopic — it is a monument. Dennis Quaid carries 14 years of development on his shoulders, playing Reagan from his thirties to his eighties with warmth, humor, and the conviction of a man who genuinely believes he is doing God's work. The film is structured through the eyes of a retired KGB agent (Jon Voight) whose grudging respect for Reagan provides the dramatic spine. The 98% audience score against an 18% critics score tells you everything: this film was made by conservatives, for conservatives, about a conservative hero. It does not pretend otherwise.

#4: The SpongeBob Movie: Search for SquarePants (2025)

STRONGLY TRADITIONAL TRAD: 43.1 WOKE: 1.3 MARGIN: +41.82 TRADITIONAL

Genre: Animation/Adventure/Comedy • Platform: Theatrical

The fourth SpongeBob theatrical outing arrives with refreshing simplicity. It tells a straightforward story about friendship and courage, delivers its moral without a lecture, and contains zero identity politics, zero DEI messaging, zero revisionism. SpongeBob wants to be a "big guy" and learns that being big is not about slaying monsters but about character. Mark Hamill's Flying Dutchman is a genuinely threatening villain who manipulates, lies, and betrays — defeated through narrative, not messaging. At 96 minutes with $167M worldwide, it proves clean children's entertainment still sells.

#5: Ne Zha 2 (2025)

STRONGLY TRADITIONAL TRAD: 38.6 WOKE: 0.0 MARGIN: +38.57 TRADITIONAL

Genre: Animation/Fantasy/Action • Platform: Theatrical

One of the most extraordinary animated films made anywhere in the past decade. Yang Yu's sequel makes the original look like a rehearsal. The father-son relationship between Li Jing and Ne Zha is the foundation: filial piety treated as unambiguous virtue, sacrifice for family as the highest expression of love, friendship built on shared struggle. The film grossed over 3 billion RMB in China in its first week. While Disney and Pixar made films about rejecting traditional expectations, Yang Yu made a movie about a boy who loves his parents so much he will fight heaven itself to protect them.

#6: Miracle (2004)

STRONGLY TRADITIONAL TRAD: 37.4 WOKE: 1.4 MARGIN: +35.98 TRADITIONAL

Genre: Drama / Sports / History • Platform: Theatrical • Director: Gavin O'Connor • Stars: Kurt Russell as Herb Brooks, Patricia Clarkson as Patti Brooks, Noah Emmerich as Craig Patrick • Runtime: 135 min • Rating: PG

Kurt Russell disappears into Herb Brooks in a performance of coiled intensity. Brooks chose players he did not like so he could coach them harder — the highest-performing teams sometimes require leaders willing to be disliked in service of the mission. The Soviet team is respected as a worthy adversary, not caricatured. The famous conditioning drills after the tie game, Brooks making them skate lines until they drop, is the film's thesis: you become what you prepare to become. This is a Disney production that Disney would be unable to make today — unambiguously about American greatness with no interest in complicating that.

#7: The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring (2001)

STRONGLY TRADITIONAL TRAD: 36.1 WOKE: 0.3 MARGIN: +35.77 TRADITIONAL

Genre: Fantasy / Adventure / Epic • Platform: Theatrical / Home Video • Director: Peter Jackson • Stars: Elijah Wood, Ian McKellen, Viggo Mortensen • Runtime: 178 min (theatrical) / 228 min (extended) • Rating: PG-13 (Epic Battle Sequences, Some Scary Images)

Released three months after 9/11, Peter Jackson's adaptation of Tolkien's unfilmable masterpiece is one of the most traditionally moral films ever made. Gandalf's line — "All we have to decide is what to do with the time that is given us" — is moral clarity rooted in a transcendent framework. Boromir's fall and redemption, Galadriel's refusal of power, Frodo and Sam's friendship: there is no identity politics, no deconstruction of the hero, no institutional critique. There is only Tolkien's moral vision rendered by filmmakers who understood it was not theirs to change. The trilogy grossed $2.9 billion worldwide.

#8: American Sniper (2014)

STRONGLY TRADITIONAL TRAD: 36.6 WOKE: 2.5 MARGIN: +34.15 TRADITIONAL

Genre: Action, Biography, Drama • Platform: Theatrical (Warner Bros.)

Clint Eastwood made this at 84, and it is among his most confident works. Bradley Cooper plays Chris Kyle as a man whose inner life is inaccessible to himself — organized around function rather than feeling. The battle sequences are technically accomplished, but Eastwood is interested in what combat decisions cost. The marriage between Chris and Taya Kyle (Sienna Miller, underrated) is the emotional spine. The film broke virtually every box office record for a war film with an $89.2M opening weekend. Eastwood ends not with a scene he invented but with footage of the real memorial service — the highway lined with flags.

#9: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (2002)

STRONGLY TRADITIONAL TRAD: 36.7 WOKE: 4.6 MARGIN: +32.06 TRADITIONAL

Genre: Fantasy / Family / Adventure / Mystery • Platform: Theatrical • Director: Chris Columbus • Stars: Daniel Radcliffe, Emma Watson, Rupert Grint • Runtime: 161 min • Rating: PG (Scary Moments, Mild Language, Fantasy Violence)

The longest and most purely faithful Harry Potter adaptation. Chris Columbus delivers a gothic mystery for children anchored in moral clarity. Dumbledore's thesis — "It is our choices, Harry, that show what we truly are" — is the clearest articulation of a traditional moral worldview: identity is not fixed, you are not the sum of your bloodline, you are what you choose to do. Kenneth Branagh's Gilderoy Lockhart is vanity given flesh. Jason Isaacs's Lucius Malfoy brings cold aristocratic contempt. At 161 minutes, Chamber of Secrets refuses to rush, and the film is better for it.

#10: Hoosiers (1986)

STRONGLY TRADITIONAL TRAD: 34.5 WOKE: 2.8 MARGIN: +31.76 TRADITIONAL

Genre: Drama / Sports • Platform: Theatrical • Director: David Anspaugh • Stars: Gene Hackman as Coach Norman Dale, Barbara Hershey as Myra Fleener, Dennis Hopper as Shooter Flatch • Runtime: 114 min • Rating: PG

If you want to explain what a traditional sports film looks like, you show them Hoosiers. Gene Hackman plays Coach Norman Dale as a man carrying something heavy — quiet in that specific way that men who have made serious mistakes tend to be quiet. He does not explain himself or seek sympathy; he just coaches. Dennis Hopper earned his only Oscar nomination as Shooter Flatch, the town drunk and father of a player, whose redemption arc is handled with more dignity than almost any depiction of alcoholism in cinema. 100% on Rotten Tomatoes. The rare case where critics and traditionalists agree completely.

#11: Exit 8 (2026)

STRONGLY TRADITIONAL TRAD: 31.6 WOKE: 0.7 MARGIN: +30.94 TRADITIONAL

Genre: Psychological Horror / Mystery / Drama • Platform: Theatrical • Director: Genki Kawamura • Stars: Kazunari Ninomiya, Yamato Kochi, Naru Asanuma • Runtime: 95 min • Rating: NR

A 2026 Japanese psychological horror film with a 97% Rotten Tomatoes score that is also one of the most traditional films we have ever scored. A man trapped in an infinite subway corridor must spot anomalies to reach Exit 8, but the loop is not a puzzle — it is a moral reckoning. Is he ready to be a father? Is he the kind of man who acts when it matters? The Walking Man, a figure who chose a false exit and abandoned a child, is the film's purest horror image: what men become when they choose escape over responsibility. Fatherhood is the highest stake. Masculine accountability is the engine. Redemption through earned action is the resolution.

#12: 13 Hours: The Secret Soldiers of Benghazi (2016)

STRONGLY TRADITIONAL TRAD: 32.3 WOKE: 1.7 MARGIN: +30.64 TRADITIONAL

Genre: Action / War / Historical Drama • Platform: Theatrical • Director: Michael Bay • Stars: John Krasinski, James Badge Dale, Pablo Schreiber • Runtime: 144 min • Rating: R (Strong Combat Violence Throughout, Bloody Images, and Language)

Michael Bay's most serious film. On September 11, 2012, six GRS contractors defied a stand-down order to defend Americans under attack in Benghazi. John Krasinski and James Badge Dale anchor a film that strips away the political argument and tells the story from the operators' perspective with documentary precision. The CIA chief (David Costabile) is not evil — he is afraid, and his fear costs lives. Bay handles the deaths of Woods and Doherty with complete dignity. The closing sequence of real photographs over the credits is the only moment that matters: remember what these men did.

#13: 12 Angry Men (1957) (1957)

STRONGLY TRADITIONAL TRAD: 30.6 WOKE: 0.0 MARGIN: +30.59 TRADITIONAL

Genre: Drama / Crime • Platform: Amazon Prime / Apple TV / YouTube Movies • Director: Sidney Lumet • Stars: Henry Fonda, Lee J. Cobb, Ed Begley • Runtime: 96 min • Rating: Not Rated (Thematic Elements, Brief Strong Language, Suitable for Ages 12+)

Sidney Lumet's feature debut is 96 minutes of men arguing in one room and is one of the greatest films ever made. Henry Fonda's Juror 8 is not a heroic orator — he asks questions, waits, lets others arrive at conclusions. His quietness is the most powerful thing on screen. Lee J. Cobb's Juror 3 tears up a photograph of his son and realizes his vote was never about the defendant. The film is a celebration of what the jury system requires: patience, reason, the courage to dissent, and the humility to change your mind. That is not woke. That is the Judeo-Christian and classical liberal tradition converging on a single point: the dignity of the individual under law.

#14: Gladiator (2000)

STRONGLY TRADITIONAL TRAD: 32.2 WOKE: 1.7 MARGIN: +30.5 TRADITIONAL

Genre: Action, Adventure, Drama • Platform: Theatrical (DreamWorks / Universal)

Twenty-five years old and still hits like a fist. Russell Crowe's Maximus is organized around duty, family, and faith. When he kneels to pray before battle, running fingers through grain, it lands as completely believable. Joaquin Phoenix's Commodus is the masterstroke: not a cartoon villain but a weak man who wants to be loved, who cannot earn respect and takes power instead, who commits atrocities from profound inadequacy. The arena sequences are spectacular, and Hans Zimmer's score makes the Roman setting mythic. A Best Picture winner whose hero fights and dies for republican virtue.

#15: Am I Racist? (2024)

STRONGLY TRADITIONAL TRAD: 33.8 WOKE: 3.7 MARGIN: +30.11 TRADITIONAL

Genre: Documentary/Comedy • Platform: Theatrical / DailyWire+

Matt Walsh does his best Borat impression, and it works more often than it does not. Going undercover as a bumbling white liberal who desperately wants to confront his racism, Walsh infiltrates DEI workshops, anti-racism training sessions, and academic conferences. The film became the highest-grossing documentary of 2024, proving that audiences are hungry for content willing to puncture progressive orthodoxy. Not every segment lands, but when it works, it works because Walsh lets the absurdity speak for itself rather than editorializing over it.

#16: Paddington 2 (2017)

STRONGLY TRADITIONAL TRAD: 32.0 WOKE: 2.1 MARGIN: +29.9 TRADITIONAL

Genre: Family Comedy Adventure • Platform: Theatrical

It might be the most morally serious film of the last twenty years. Brightly colored and funny and starring a CGI bear who gets into scrapes with marmalade, Paddington 2 is making a quiet, consistent, deeply conservative argument: that kindness is a form of strength, that communities are built on small decencies, that being good is hard and worth doing. Hugh Grant gives one of the best comic performances of the century as the villain Phoenix Buchanan. The prison sequences, in which Paddington reforms hardened criminals through marmalade and manners, are not naive — they are aspirational.

#17: Toy Story (1995)

STRONGLY TRADITIONAL TRAD: 30.1 WOKE: 0.5 MARGIN: +29.62 TRADITIONAL

Genre: Animation / Adventure / Comedy / Family • Platform: Theatrical / Disney+ • Director: John Lasseter • Stars: Tom Hanks, Tim Allen, Don Rickles • Runtime: 81 min • Rating: G (All Ages)

Pixar's first feature is not just a landmark of computer animation; it is a deeply traditional story about the things that matter most. At 81 minutes, not a single one wastes time on ideology. The film knows exactly what it is about: loyalty, sacrifice, and earning your place. Woody's jealousy, Buzz's identity crisis, and their eventual friendship through shared adversity — the rivalry-to-brotherhood arc is done with more economy and emotional precision than films twice its length. The G rating is not a limitation. It is a commitment.

#18: The Death of Robin Hood (2026)

STRONGLY TRADITIONAL TRAD: 34.5 WOKE: 5.9 MARGIN: +28.56 TRADITIONAL

Genre: Thriller / Drama / Historical • Platform: Theatrical • Director: Michael Sarnoski • Stars: Hugh Jackman, Jodie Comer, Bill Skarsgard • Runtime: 122 min • Rating: R (Strong Bloody Violence, Language, Brief Sexual Content)

A24 did not make a woke Robin Hood. They made a medieval Christian film about a mass murderer who finds redemption through confession, forgiveness, and sacrificial death. Hugh Jackman plays an aging, broken Robin Hood confronting the weight of the lives he has taken. Jodie Comer, as a nun who becomes his confessor, forces him to face the man he has been. Michael Sarnoski takes sin seriously, treats forgiveness as the hardest thing a person can do, and ends with genuine grace. The film is rated R and earns every minute of its 122-minute runtime.

#19: How to Train Your Dragon (2025)

STRONGLY TRADITIONAL TRAD: 33.2 WOKE: 4.7 MARGIN: +28.5 TRADITIONAL

Genre: Family/Adventure • Platform: Theatrical

Dean DeBlois insisted on full creative control for the live-action remake, and it shows. The father-son relationship between Stoick and Hiccup is the film's emotional centerpiece: a boy who cannot be the warrior his father wants, a father who learns that strength takes forms he did not expect. The dragon-flying sequences are genuinely thrilling. The film earns its traditional score through its treatment of family obligation, earned courage, and the idea that understanding your enemy is not weakness but wisdom — all delivered through spectacle rather than lecture.

#20: A Great Awakening (2026)

STRONGLY TRADITIONAL TRAD: 28.7 WOKE: 0.3 MARGIN: +28.35 TRADITIONAL

Genre: History / Drama / Faith • Platform: Theatrical • Director: Joshua Enck • Stars: John Paul Sneed as Benjamin Franklin, Jonathan Blair as George Whitefield, Zachary Amos • Runtime: 129 min • Rating: PG-13

Joshua Enck's historical drama about the friendship between George Whitefield and Benjamin Franklin is one of the most sincere faith-based films of 2026. John Paul Sneed and Jonathan Blair bring genuine chemistry to the Whitefield-Franklin partnership — one of history's most interesting odd couples. The film treats the Great Awakening as a genuine spiritual movement that changed the course of American history, without irony, without apology. Take your family. Take your small group. Take the skeptic in your life who thinks faith stories are all saccharine nonsense.

#21: Saving Private Ryan (1998)

STRONGLY TRADITIONAL TRAD: 30.8 WOKE: 2.5 MARGIN: +28.3 TRADITIONAL

Genre: Drama, War • Platform: Theatrical (DreamWorks / Paramount)

The first twenty-five minutes of Saving Private Ryan are among the most important in the history of American cinema — not because they are technically impressive, though they are that, but because they do what almost no war film before or since has done: they show what it actually costs. The Omaha Beach sequence is not spectacle. It is witness. Tom Hanks's Captain Miller leads a squad behind enemy lines to retrieve a single paratrooper whose three brothers have been killed in action. The mission is strategically irrational. The film argues, without ever stating it, that some things are worth doing because they are right, not because they are efficient.

#22: Rocky (1976)

STRONGLY TRADITIONAL TRAD: 29.5 WOKE: 1.4 MARGIN: +28.14 TRADITIONAL

Genre: Drama / Sports • Platform: Theatrical • Director: John G. Avildsen • Stars: Sylvester Stallone as Rocky Balboa, Talia Shire as Adrian, Burt Young as Paulie • Runtime: 120 min • Rating: PG

Fifty years old and it still works. Sylvester Stallone wrote himself a part — he was broke, unknown, and refused to sell the script without being cast as the lead. Rocky is about something real: a man of no particular talent or education who, when given one impossible shot, proves to himself that he belongs in the ring. The relationship with Adrian is tender, awkward, and earned. The training montage is the most imitated in cinema history because it works: discipline, structure, miles of roadwork, thousands of steps up those Philadelphia museum stairs. You become what you prepare to become.

#23: Sound of Hope: The Story of Possum Trot (2024)

STRONGLY TRADITIONAL TRAD: 29.8 WOKE: 2.0 MARGIN: +27.82 TRADITIONAL

Genre: Biography / Drama • Platform: Theatrical • Director: Joshua Weigel • Stars: Demetrius Grosse, Nika King, Elizabeth Mitchell • Runtime: 130 min • Rating: PG-13 (Thematic elements including child abuse and neglect, brief language)

The story of Possum Trot, Texas, is one of the most extraordinary in American religious life. A small church in a town most Americans cannot find on a map. Twenty-two families. Seventy-seven children adopted from the foster care system. Demetrius Grosse and Nika King lead a cast that treats faith as the engine of impossible generosity. The film does not shy away from the difficulty — children with trauma, families stretched to breaking, moments where everything seems lost — but the throughline is unwavering: love, organized and persistent and rooted in something larger than the self, changes lives.

#24: Happy Gilmore 2 (2025)

STRONGLY TRADITIONAL TRAD: 31.2 WOKE: 3.5 MARGIN: +27.77 TRADITIONAL

Genre: Sports Comedy • Platform: Netflix • Director: Kyle Newacheck • Stars: Adam Sandler, Julie Bowen, Christopher McDonald • Runtime: 1h 58m • Rating: R

Twenty-nine years is a long time between sequels. Most of those films fail. Happy Gilmore 2 does something most cannot manage: it finds a reason to revisit the character that is emotionally honest rather than merely nostalgic. Adam Sandler plays Happy as a man who has grown up but not grown out — still the same temper, still the same love for his grandmother, now facing middle age with the same tools he had at twenty-two. Julie Bowen returns as Virginia, and their dynamic has deepened into something resembling an actual adult relationship. Rated R. On Netflix.

#25: Solo Leveling: ReAwakening (2024)

STRONGLY TRADITIONAL TRAD: 28.4 WOKE: 1.3 MARGIN: +27.09 TRADITIONAL

Genre: Animation/Action/Fantasy • Platform: Theatrical

Two things stitched together: a rushed 80-minute recap of Season 1 and a spectacular 40-minute preview of Season 2. The first part is mediocre. The second part is genuinely thrilling. For parents wondering whether to let their teenager watch the anime film that has dominated streaming charts, the answer is straightforward: Solo Leveling contains zero sexual content, zero woke messaging, and zero deconstruction of the hero. It is a pure power-fantasy action anime built on earned strength, monster hunting, and the oldest heroic arc in the book: the weak become strong through sacrifice and determination.

What the Data Tells Us

Twenty-five films. All 25 scored STRONGLY TRADITIONAL. Not a single WOKE LEAN or MIXED verdict in the group. The average margin is +32.5 traditional. The average woke score is 2.2 out of 100. The average traditional score is 34.7 out of 100. These are not films that merely avoid progressive messaging. These are films constructed on a different moral foundation entirely.

The genres represented tell their own story. Biblical dramas (The Passion of the Christ). War films (American Sniper, 13 Hours, Saving Private Ryan, Fury). Sports underdog stories (Miracle, Hoosiers, Rocky). Faith-based biographies (Reagan, Sound of Hope, A Great Awakening). Fantasy epics built on moral clarity (The Lord of the Rings, Harry Potter). Family animation that values character over messaging (SpongeBob, Toy Story, Paddington 2). And then the wild cards: Exit 8, a Japanese psychological horror film about fatherhood and moral accountability that scored a 97% on Rotten Tomatoes. Am I Racist?, Matt Walsh's guerrilla documentary that became the highest-grossing documentary of 2024. Gladiator, a Best Picture winner whose hero fights and dies for republican virtue.

The lesson is not complicated. Audiences want stories about courage, sacrifice, redemption, and moral clarity. When studios provide those stories, audiences show up. The Passion of the Christ ($612M on a $30M budget). American Sniper ($547M worldwide). Gladiator ($465M). Saving Private Ryan ($482M). The Lord of the Rings trilogy ($2.9B). These are not niche films. They are among the most commercially successful films in cinema history. The audience for traditional values in entertainment is not a market segment. It is the market, and it has been systematically underserved for two decades.

The data does not lie. The films on this list exist because someone, somewhere, decided to make a film about things that matter without apologizing for it. More of that, please.
